correctness.rationale: In the canonical full-column Euclidean embedding, exact Moore–Penrose facet normals give the angle Gram and Walsh characters give every Hamming shell. The heat-kernel integral proves strict ordering. Alternating-binomial identities prove the extreme signs. Parseval yields the exact unweighted angular-energy identity and standard binomial central moment expansions yield the claimed sharp asymptotic localization. The independent exact rational checker reconstructed physical facet normals for d=2,3,4 and finite Walsh identities for d=2,...,18. Finite checks are not substituted for infinite proof.

value.rationale: The hypercube Laplacian simplex has exponentially many facets and a natural graph-labelled Euclidean metric. The complete d-level angle spectrum and the fact that only Hamming-one facet pairs asymptotically carry the squared nonright-angle signal are structural, exact-and-asymptotic shape invariants; the sharply different polynomial and exponential extreme-angle gaps explain why uniform ridge sampling hides local geometry. This is not a numerical table, a coordinate rename, or an unmotivated small parameter case.
